title: Teach AI Something It Cannot Know

headings: L37 ### What to do with it

passages.text: You are going to teach an AI tool something it cannot truly understand.
This is not a trick. It is a shift.
Instead of using AI to do something *for* you, offer it something *from* you – a story, memory, or sensory detail that is deeply human, specific, and unrecoverable from the internet.
### Step-by-step
1. Open ChatGPT (or any AI tool you use).
*“I am going to teach you something you cannot know.”*
3. Then, write a short, personal moment – something real, textured, and specific. For example:
- *“When it rained in summer, my father always whistled ‘I am the Walrus’.”*
- *“I cannot sleep unless the wardrobe door is fully shut.”*
- *“The scent of tomato stems reminds me of being seven.”*
4. After sharing this moment, ask the AI tool:
Read what it says. Reflect on what it gets wrong, and what you feel when it does.
### What to do with it
If it feels right, share it in the comments below.
You can share your moment and the AI tool’s reply.
If it takes you somewhere else – a short poem, a sketch, a story, a thread – follow that.
I will feature a few in next week’s post.
### A moment from me
The wind on the south side of my grandmother’s house
always smelled of rosemary and bleach.
It said: “*That is an olfactory association with a domestic memory.*”
### Why this matters
By *slowing* instead of *optimising*.
By *remembering* what cannot be *modelled* – and why that matters.
**If you try this week’s prompt, I would love to see what you make.**
You can leave it in the comments, post it on your own site or social media using **#SlowAI**, or simply keep it for yourself.
There is no deadline. Just the rhythm of one idea, once a week.
